leads.title: Penal Code of Cuba (1979) - repeal of Social Defence Code
leads.documents: Decriminalization of private, adult, non-commercial consensual same-sex relations age 16+; repealed Code that called 'homosexual practices' a 'social threat'.
leads.detail: Article text: 'The Social Defence Code, which characterized "homosexual practices" as a "social threat"... was repealed in 1979 by the Penal Code of Cuba. This Code did not criminalize homosexuality per se.' No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Cuba Penal Code Article 359(1)
leads.documents: Residual criminalization of 'public display of their homosexual condition' and 'homosexual requests' - shows enforcement tool after 1979.
leads.detail: Article text: 'Article 359(1) criminalized those who made "public display of their homosexual condition"... The crime of "public display" was repealed in 1987 and... amended in 1997 to refer only to "sexual" requests.' No URL visible.

leads.title: People's Supreme Court ruling (1975)
leads.documents: Court ruling in favor of marginalized gay artists claiming compensation and reinstatement - initial change in official attitudes.
leads.detail: Article text: 'In 1975, the People's Supreme Court found in favor of a group of marginalised gay artists who were claiming compensation and reinstatement in their place of work.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Constitution of Cuba - Article 36 and 2019 Constitution
leads.documents: Constitutional definition of marriage as between man and woman until repealed in February 2019 referendum; current text based on free will and equality.
leads.detail: Article text: 'Until 2019, Article 36 contained language defining marriage as between a man and a woman. This was repealed in a February 2019 referendum.' No URL visible.

leads.title: National Assembly of People's Power - Draft Constitution Article 68 (2018)
leads.documents: Government legislative attempt to recognize same-sex marriage in July 2018 draft, withdrawn Dec 2018 after evangelical pressure.
leads.detail: Article text: 'In July 2018, the National Assembly approved a new draft constitution which recognized same-sex marriage in Article 68... National Assembly withdrew the language on 18 December 2018.' No URL visible.

leads.title: 2022 Cuban Family Code referendum / Union of Jurists of Cuba draft
leads.documents: Legal recognition of same-sex marriage, unions, same-sex adoption and non-commercial surrogacy; anti-discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity.
leads.detail: Article text: 'Following the 2022 Cuban Family Code referendum, there is legal recognition of the right to marriage... same-sex adoption and non-commercial surrogacy' and 'government announced... Union of Jurists of Cuba was working on the new Family Code' and 'referendum... took place in September 2022, with the referendum passing.' No URL visible.

leads.title: National Center for Sex Education (CENESEX) / National Commission on Sex Education
leads.documents: State rights machinery headed by Mariela Castro; 1986 opinion that homosexuality was sexual orientation, education campaigns, Pride parades in Havana.
leads.detail: Article text: 'Educational campaigns... implemented by the National Center for Sex Education (locally known as "CENESEX"), headed by Mariela Castro' and 'In 1986, the National Commission on Sex Education publicly opined that homosexuality was a sexual orientation'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Human Rights Watch report on 1997 crackdown
leads.documents: Documented enforcement incident: heightened harassment, raids on gay nightclubs, beatings and detentions.
leads.detail: Article text: 'According to a Human Rights Watch report, "the government [in 1997] ... heightened harassment of homosexuals, raiding several nightclubs known to have gay clientele and allegedly beating and detaining dozens of patrons."' No URL visible.

leads.title: United States government report on El Periquiton raid
leads.documents: Documented enforcement: fines, threats of imprisonment for public homosexuality, beating of Cuban clientele in Havana raid involving Pedro Almodovar.
leads.detail: Article text: 'According to a United States government report, Cuban customers of the club were fined and warned of imprisonment if they did not stop publicly displaying their homosexuality... Many of the Cuban gay and lesbian clientele were reportedly beaten by police.' No URL visible.

leads.title: BBC report (2004) and Miami Herald report (2019)
leads.documents: BBC documents police campaign specifically against travestis/transvestites for cross-dressing; Miami Herald documents 2019 state cancellation of anti-homophobia march and arrest of 3 independent marchers.
leads.detail: Article text: BBC: '"Cuban police have once again launched a campaign against homosexuals, specifically directed at travestis (transvestites) whom they are arresting if they are dressed in women's clothing."' Miami Herald: CENESEX canceled 12th annual march against homophobia due to 'international and regional tensions' / Christian resistance; 'At least three were arrested'. No URLs visible.
